Class WhoWebSecurityAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.autoconfigure.WhoWebSecurityAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(after={WhoSpringSecurityAutoConfiguration.class,WhoJwtAutoConfiguration.class,WhoApiKeyAutoConfiguration.class,WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration.class,WhoPasskeyAutoConfiguration.class,WhoOidcAutoConfiguration.class}, afterName="org.springframework.boot.security.oauth2.server.resource.autoconfigure.OAuth2ResourceServerAutoConfiguration", beforeName={"org.springframework.boot.security.autoconfigure.web.servlet.ServletWebSecurityAutoConfiguration","org.springframework.boot.security.oauth2.server.resource.autoconfigure.web.OAuth2ResourceServerWebSecurityAutoConfiguration","org.springframework.boot.security.autoconfigure.actuate.web.servlet.ManagementWebSecurityAutoConfiguration","org.springframework.boot.security.oauth2.client.autoconfigure.servlet.OAuth2ClientWebSecurityAutoConfiguration"}) @ConditionalOnWebApplication(type=SERVLET) @ConditionalOnClass(name={"org.jwcarman.who.spring.security.WhoSecurity","org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain","org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity"}) @ConditionalOnMissingBean(org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain.class) public class WhoWebSecurityAutoConfiguration extends Object
who's default SecurityFilterChain, in place of Spring Boot's: every sign-in method on the classpath (WhoSecurity.all()), the public paths open to signed-out requests, CSRF for every request that brings a session, Actuator's health endpoint open as Boot's own chain leaves it, and every other request signed in. It backs off as soon as the application defines a SecurityFilterChain of its own, and takes the place of the default chains Spring Boot would register: form login, the resource server's, Actuator's and oauth2Login's.

  • Method Details

    • whoSecurityFilterChain

      @Bean @Order(2147483642) public org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain whoSecurityFilterChain(org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity http, WhoPublicPaths publicPaths, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<PasswordlessLoginMethod> browserMethods)
      The default chain.

      Without a browser sign-in method who gives no request a session, so CSRF then ignores the requests that bring none, and a signed-out client may post to a public path. A request that brings a session, which something other than who may have started, keeps its CSRF check.

      Parameters:
      http - the chain builder
      publicPaths - the paths open to signed-out requests
      browserMethods - the browser sign-in methods
      Returns:
      the chain
